newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says foreign reserves at over $3.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says foreign reserves at over $3.5 bln.

text.p: Algeria's Central Bank governor Abdelwahab Keramane said on Sunday foreign reserves reached more than $3.5 billion this year, the top level of reserves reached since 1981.

"The reserves exceeded for the second time $3.5 billion since 1981," Keramane was quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS as addressing the government-appointed Transitional National Council (CNT), a parliament-like body.
He said Algeria's reserves had reached such level only in 1981 when the oil crude prices surged in the wake of the first war between Iraq and Iran.
The reserves amounted to $2.5 billion at the end of last March compared to $2.11 billion at the end of last December.

Keramane did not give figure of the crude oil windfall from the increase of oil prices in last months but the government said last July Algerian oil prices averaging $20.2 per barrel in the first five months of 1996 against $17.9 per barrel in the same period last year.
Keramane, in a rare appearance by the country's bank chief, addresseed on Sunday the CNT on the country's monetary and financial situation.
It was the second time that an Algerian central bank had come out to an assembly to talk about the country's finances.
Keramane's predecessor Hadj Nacer Roustomi Aberrahmane was forced to appear before the parliament later in 1990 to calm down angry deputies over a then disputed gold reserves swap.
The parliament was dissolved early in January 1992 by president Chadli Benjedid before he stepped down seven days later.
